module_title: Advanced Analysis - Biosphere Zoning, MAB, and Wildlife Laws
introduction: This advanced level analyzes the scientific zoning of Biospheres, UNESCO's international recognition framework, and the legal backbone of Indian conservation (The Wildlife Protection Act).

core_concepts.title: Biosphere Reserve Zoning System
core_concepts.description: Divided into 3 zones: 1. Core Zone (innermost, strictly protected, no human interference), 2. Buffer Zone (surrounds the core, limited tourism, education, and research allowed), 3. Transition Zone (outermost, sustainable human settlements and agriculture permitted).

core_concepts.title: UNESCO MAB Programme
core_concepts.description: India has 18 Biosphere Reserves. Out of these, 12 are internationally recognized under UNESCO's 'Man and the Biosphere' (MAB) network. The 12th and latest addition is the 'Panna' Biosphere Reserve in Madhya Pradesh.

core_concepts.title: Wildlife Protection Act (1972)
core_concepts.description: The most critical environmental law in India. It contains 6 Schedules. Animals listed in 'Schedule 1' and 'Part II of Schedule 2' (like Tigers, Rhinos, Great Indian Bustards, Pangolins) are provided absolute protection, and hunting them attracts the highest penalties.

core_concepts.title: Namdapha National Park
core_concepts.description: Located in Arunachal Pradesh, it is unique for having a massive altitudinal variation. It is the only park in India featuring 4 distinct vegetation zones (from tropical to alpine) and is famous for the Flying Squirrel.

important_entities.name: Khangchendzonga National Park
important_entities.significance: Located in Sikkim, it is India's only 'Mixed' (having both outstanding natural and cultural significance) UNESCO World Heritage Site.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve is not just in Kerala. It straddles the border of BOTH 'Kerala and Tamil Nadu'. If an option lists both, choose it.
Under the WPA 1972, 'State Governments' have the power to declare an area as a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary, not just the Central Government.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Nilgiri, Nanda Devi, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC frequently tests the zoning rules: Remember that 'Research and Education' are typically allowed in the Buffer Zone, while the Core Zone is off-limits.
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, recall that critically endangered species like the Great Indian Bustard (GIB) and Snow Leopard are protected under Schedule 1 of the WPA 1972.
